question: Does the unchanged strictly-positive registered planar-extent support rule preserve exact open-roster correspondence when complete 3RScan surfaces are replaced by target-conditioned points actually observed in real SceneNN RGB-D frames?

source_selector.inventory: Previously materialized provider XML inventory only; no scene 096 PLY, trajectory, RGB, depth, score, or support value may be opened before admission.
source_selector.ordering: Ascending three-digit SceneNN scene ID; within a scene, ascending numeric instance ID.
source_selector.normalized_target_label: lowercase text with whitespace removed must match door followed by zero or more digits; door mat and other compounds are excluded
source_selector.stop_rule: Select the first unconsumed scene with at least four qualifying door instances, then stop.

provider.name: SceneNN
provider.sensor: Asus Xtion PRO consumer RGB-D camera
provider.world_coordinate_contract: trajectory.log maps camera points into the reconstructed scene frame; SceneNN aligns the floor with the x-z plane, so +/−y is the upright axis and only its unoriented line is used
provider.license_boundary: Free for educational and research use; contact SceneNN before commercial use. BlindAssist stores local research assets only and does not redistribute raw payloads.

allowed_inputs: provider mesh vertices, triangle faces and instance labels
pre_rgbd_selector.pair_ranking: Maximum camera-centre baseline, then minimum visible target pixels, then minimum visibility ratio, then earlier reference and query frames.

renderer.implementation: unchanged CuPy CUDA triangle rasterizer from l10_scenenn_visible_portal_transfer.py
renderer.near_plane_face_rule: Reject a face unless all vertices are beyond the near plane.
renderer.visibility_rule: target depth finite and no farther than full-scene depth plus 0.005 m

pre_rgbd_selector.failure_semantics: If any of the four frozen targets lacks one qualifying frame pair, record NOT_EVALUABLE. Do not substitute a scene or change selector values after RGB-D access.

observation_carrier.mask: provider instance mesh z-buffer-visible pixels for the frozen target
observation_carrier.depth: synchronized SceneNN sensor depth at the selected trajectory frame
observation_carrier.depth_consistency_rule: retain a masked nonzero sensor point only when its depth differs from rendered target depth by at most 0.08 m
observation_carrier.point_cap_rule: if needed, retain 4096 deterministic evenly spaced points in raster traversal order
observation_carrier.portal_frame: reference observation centroid; principal horizontal direction in SceneNN x-z floor plane; y upright
observation_carrier.surface_score: negative symmetric median nearest-neighbour distance between reference and query observed points
observation_carrier.existence_support: strictly positive convex-hull intersection after projection into the reference observation upright portal frame; no IoU magnitude threshold
observation_carrier.zero_assignment: strict reciprocal row and column maximum of surface score, then positive-support predicate

forbidden_after_rgbd_access: change source scene or target instances
change depth consistency tolerance or point limits
change portal frame, surface score, reciprocity, support predicate, or scenarios
select a subset of the four frozen targets
claim_boundary: A pass is provider-disjoint real consumer-RGB-D Development evidence that the unchanged positive registered planar-extent support predicate can operate on privileged target-conditioned partial depth observations rather than complete provider surfaces. SceneNN instance masks, reconstruction and camera trajectory remain privileged; the sensor is not a phone and the query target proposal is truth-conditioned. This is not raw-phone perception, door detection, a doorway aperture, named entrance, venue ownership, public access, traversability, approach waypoint, arrival, HANDOFF_READY, user benefit, deployment, or mobility-safety evidence.
